Here are the standard opening lines of **Chapter 1 of *To Kill a Mockingbird***, which you can use for your close-reading exercise:

> **When Jem was nearly ten, our father told us once and for all to stop playing the Boo Radley game whenever we discussed it. Up to then, we—Jem, Scout, and Dill—had been more or less under the impression that Boo was an evil omen: as long as we never bothered him, he would never bother us. But when Atticus became so angry that he threw his newspaper onto the floor and his glasses on the table, we knew something was wrong. We were sitting on the porch, a rocking chair squeaking rhythmically, when Atticus said, "Now listen here, you two. That man has as much right to his privacy as you have to yours."**

*(Note: The exact wording can vary very slightly between editions, but this is the universally recognized start of the narrative voice, typically featuring Scout's point of view being established before any historical context.)*
